audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 with Akshan on all seven rows matches a 52.76% win rate over 1503 games against a champion with no mobility spell at any point in the game. The two layers agree row for row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike was built on 'a dash-enabling lethality item' — Akshan has no such item and no dash. The level 6 spike was built on Rite of the Arcane being a global execute.
audit.why: Rite of the Arcane is 5000 range, deals no execute damage, and immobilizes Xerath himself for the duration; it is also a channel, so any CC cancels it. Akshan's mobility is Heroic Swing off terrain, 800 range on an 18s-to-12s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Level 3 spike is Heroic Swing crossing his 750-range Arcanopulse; level 6 is Xerath rooting himself to channel; first item is the three-hit string becoming lethal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content said Eye of Destruction roots you and called Shocking Orb 'his short root'. The decisive fact — that Rite of the Arcane immobilizes Xerath and is interruptible — was never stated.
audit.why: Eye of Destruction slows only (Riot text: 'slowing and dealing magic damage'; stronger slow in the middle). Shocking Orb is the stun, 1050 range, 13/12.5/12/11.5/11. Rite of the Arcane 'immobilizes himself' and carries the channel flag, so it is the single largest punish window in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Shocking Orb is his only CC; Eye of Destruction is a slow; when Rite of the Arcane starts, Xerath cannot move and any CC ends it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page tracked Shocking Orb without ever giving its cooldown.
audit.why: 13 seconds at rank 1 falling only to 11 at rank 5 — a dodged orb is a fixed, countable window, which is exactly the kind of number this advice needed.

edits.before: Kit completion at level 3 gives you a reliable way to close distance and punish his cast time.
edits.after: Kit complete at level 3: Heroic Swing crosses the gap his 750-range Arcanopulse cannot hold.

edits.before: Continued dash pressure keeps him from safely poking, extending your lead.
edits.after: Constant swing pressure stops him ever free-casting the poke he needs.

edits.before: Zero escape tools mean overextensions are consistently punished in your favor.
edits.after: With no escape, one Shocking Orb miss is a free 13 seconds to punish him.

edits.before: Comeuppance counters his global execute ultimate, keeping level 6 in your favor.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane roots him in place for the channel — that is your window.

edits.before: Lethality-enabled dashes close the gap even faster, denying his range advantage.
edits.after: Your first item burst kills him inside the 13 seconds Shocking Orb is down.

edits.before: Immobility remains his fatal flaw, letting your flanks win skirmishes into the late game.
edits.after: He never gains mobility, so a camouflage flank still ends him in any late skirmish.

edits.before: Xerath has zero mobility and telegraphed skillshots, so once E is unlocked you can weave through his Arcanopulse/Eye of Destruction and close the gap to punish him hard before he can reposition.
edits.after: Xerath has zero mobility and telegraphed skillshots, so once Heroic Swing is unlocked you cross his 750-range Arcanopulse — Eye of Destruction only slows, so the whiffed Shocking Orb is the real opening.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane is a global execute threat, but Comeuppance directly answers it — if he ults a squishy ally you can race in and either save them or punish his commitment while he's locked in animation.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane is 5000 range, not global, and it immobilizes Xerath for the whole channel — any CC cancels it. When it starts, he cannot move: swing onto him and he either dies or throws the ult away.

edits.before: Once you have a dash-enabling lethality item, closing the distance on Xerath becomes trivial — his only real defense is range, and once that's gone he has no escape at all.
edits.after: Once your first item lands, one three-hit string plus the swing's autos is most of his health bar — his only defence is range, and Heroic Swing is 800 of it for 15 seconds.

edits.before: Xerath's poke damage scales hard, but he's still rooted in place when casting and has no dash — camouflage flanks and quick all-ins shut down his ability to kite or free-cast in skirmishes.
edits.after: Xerath's poke scales hard, but he still stands still to cast and has no dash — camouflage flanks and quick all-ins stop him free-casting, and Shocking Orb is his one answer at 11 seconds.

edits.before: Xerath's kit is entirely built around uninterrupted range, and he has no mobility spell whatsoever, so once you have E to close distance at level 3 the matchup swings hard your way — dodge his skillshots, eat some poke, and punish every cast with a dive. Even in levels 1-2 his damage isn't lethal enough to punish your approach if you play the minion wave correctly.
edits.after: Xerath is built around uninterrupted range and has no mobility spell at all, so once Heroic Swing is up at level 3 the matchup swings your way. Shocking Orb is his only CC and the only thing that turns poke into a kill — dodge it and you have 13 seconds. Levels 1-2 his damage cannot stop your approach if you use the minion wave for cover.

edits.before: His Rite of the Arcane threatens global picks, but Comeuppance answers this well by letting you race to save allies or punish the commitment. Keep applying pressure — every time he tries to poke from range, you're one dash away from ending the fight, since he has nothing to escape with besides his short root.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane is a 5000-range barrage, not a global snipe, and Xerath is immobile and interruptible while it runs — the moment he casts it he is the easiest kill on the map. Keep the pressure on: he escapes with nothing but a 1050-range stun, so every poke attempt is a swing away from a kill.

edits.before: Xerath becomes a serious poke and pick threat in teamfights with a full build, but 1v1 he remains completely immobile — camouflage engages and E swing-ins let you close the gap before he can land his damage, and once you're on top of him there's no counterplay left in his kit.
edits.after: Xerath is a serious poke and pick threat in teamfights with a full build, but he never buys mobility — camouflage flanks and swing-ins close the gap before he lands damage, and once you are on him only Shocking Orb stands between you and a dead artillery mage.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.

notes: Two factual errors removed: Rite of the Arcane described as a global execute (it is 5000 range, no execute, and immobilizes Xerath himself), and Eye of Destruction described as a root (it slows; the stun is Shocking Orb). Also removed 'dash-enabling lethality item' — Akshan has no dash and no such item. The biggest addition is that Rite of the Arcane roots Xerath and is a channel any CC cancels, which was absent from every layer. tldr, winCon, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.wave, breakdown.late, ahead, tradeGood and tradeBad are shared Akshan boilerplate and remain templated; I could not ground them further in Xerath's kit without repeating the Shocking Orb point already carried by focus, cooldowns and the dos/donts.
